subject.title: fix: workflow sanity audit passes on main

question: Should the fallback GitHub App be authorized for `contents: read`, and can its primary-token-failure recovery path be demonstrated before this expanded token scope lands?
rationale: Only workflow/App owners can confirm the fallback installation’s granted permissions or safely arrange a controlled primary-token failure; source review and ordinary successful runs cannot establish that recovery contract.

options.title: Confirm and prove fallback access
options.body: Authorize the fallback App for repository contents read if intended, then attach a redacted controlled-run transcript showing fallback token creation, configuration read, and successful labeling.

options.title: Keep fallback least-privilege
options.body: Remove the fallback `contents: read` request and redesign the configuration-read step so recovery does not require this additional token scope.

options.title: Pause the permission expansion
options.body: Leave the workflow unchanged until the fallback App’s permission boundary and recovery behavior can be owned by the relevant automation team.

recommendation.title: Confirm and prove fallback access
recommendation.body: Authorize the fallback App for repository contents read if intended, then attach a redacted controlled-run transcript showing fallback token creation, configuration read, and successful labeling.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor can supply branch-side evidence and route the remaining App-installation confirmation to the workflow owner, although current-main ownership is not established here.
